FIDELITY (l.1877-1886): (i) X = closedBall 0 1 with the open disc carrying hypDist. hypDist is mathlib's UpperHalfPlane distance through the inverse Cayley transform, and cosh_hypDist proves it is the Poincaré formula. (ii) G = HypIsom is the group of ALL hypDist-preserving permutations, which is the paper's 'group of isometries'. It is classified as the maps z -> (u s(z)+a)/(1+conj(a) u s(z)) and acts on X by the continuous extension: a MulAction plus ContinuousConstSMul, i.e. by homeomorphisms. Faithfulness and rigidity are proved on both the open and the closed disc, so AnalyticStructure holds and X is locally unloopable (the standing hypothesis of l.1660). (iii) take_closed_unit_disc proves: sing(M) = S; IsTame (Tame's real def:singular_manifold_tame_admits via isTame_of_isDevelopingMapOf); a developing map of M̃ = MaxBranchedCover (sing M) y0 exists; the singular points of M̃ are exactly the points over sing M; EVERY developing map is injective; at each singular x, D(x) lies on the unit circle; and in every neighbourhood of x there is an open U, homeomorphic to {r < r0} in DInfty with x going to the apex, such that D(U) = horoSet (D x) τ with τ > 0 and D(U) is not open in X. Every assertion is at least as strong as the paper's, and the three REPORT findings say where it is stronger. The last sentence reuses GX.not_isOpen_horodisc_insert as asked. horodisc is the genuine Busemann horodisc {|ξ-z|^2 < t(1-|z|^2)}: horodisc_eq_ball proves it is the Euclidean disc of radius t/(1+t) internally tangent at ξ, so it is not trivialised. (iv) Nothing the proof needs is assumed. The cusp-wise hypothesis behind injective_of_isCuspDev and the continuity of D is discharged inside exists_developing from exists_end_lift, and the classical GX.developing_theorem is genuinely used. HYPOTHESES: IsCuspedHyperbolic reads 'finite volume complete hyperbolic metric on M∖S' as three things: a (Isom ℍ, ℍ)-structure; Thurston/Goldman completeness (every developing map of the universal cover is a covering map); and a cusp chart at each s ∈ S. A cusp chart is V ≅ ball(0, e^{-2πc}) with s -> 0, on which w -> φ⁻¹(e^{2πiw}), Im w > c, is locally g • Cayley in the charts of M∖S. The paper's hypotheses imply this through the thick-thin decomposition and the hyperbolic Hopf-Rinow theorem, neither of which is built. I tried to satisfy it: the punctured-disc cusp ℍ/<z+1> meets every field, so it is not unsatisfiable, and it is not circular, since sing = S and injectivity are proved from it and not assumed. The REPORT honestly sets the row to 'partial' and leaves it unmarked, gives the reading in SCOPE (b) and as a question, and lists M Hausdorff, locally path-connected, first countable and connected as weakenings (all implied by 'genus g surface'). DEC-71 does not explicitly accept the finite-volume => cusps reading, so partial plus a question is the right DEC-27 status and not an avoidable weakening.
